title: Add alt text to images & charts for improved accessibility
body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [X] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Add a way for developers to add alt text to commands such as `st.image` and chart objects.

### Why?

For accessibility reasons, images, charts, and other visualizations should always have [alt text](https://www.w3.org/WAI/tutorials/images/tips/) that describes the content. 

### How?

This should probably be a parameter that the developer can set since we can't automatically generate alt text (even though this might be a cool LLM application 😉 ). Maybe just a parameter `alt` or `alt_text` or `alternative_text` that accepts a string. 

Elements for which we could/should add this:
- st.image
- st.dataframe and st.table (see [this article on accessible tables](https://www.albany.edu/web-services/accessibility/accessibility-basics/5-creating-accessible-tables))
- all [chart elements](https://docs.streamlit.io/develop/api-reference/charts)

Note that some of these elements also have other parameters to describe the content (e.g. `st.image` has a `caption` parameter), so we'd have to see how these two work together. 

### Additional Context

_No response_

The caption and the alt text are for different purposes. While the caption helps users relate to the text, the alt text provides a textual alternative for screen readers, describing the image and making the content accessible to all. # Update

We haven't started working on this yet, but we definitely want to have it and given the big amount of upvotes recently, I guess we'll prioritize this in the short- or medium-term. I also think this should be relatively easy to spec out and implement, so no major risks other than other projects taking up our time.
Any update on this? It would be great to be able to provide alt text for blind users without caption for sighted users.

I think we should apply this to `st.image`, `st.dataframe` and `st.data_editor` and all chart commands. It should be one parameter that can be used across all of them, probably either:

1. `alt` or `alt_text` or something similar: standard and very well understood, but technically the HTML alt attribute only exists for images
2. `accessible_description` or `accessible_text` or something similar: bit more generic and potentially more correct than `alt`; need to check with accessibility guidelines which term is correct here though

And then under the hood we should set whichever HTML attribute is the "best" one for that specific element. For images probably the HTML `alt` attribute, for dataframes/charts probably one of the `aria` attributes. Need to look into accessibility best practices what works well.

This is a feature enhancement request to add alt text support to `st.image`, `st.dataframe`/`st.table`, and all chart elements for improved accessibility. Currently, `st.image` uses a generic key as the `alt` attribute on `` tags (see `ImageList.tsx`), and chart elements have no alt text or ARIA description support in their protobuf definitions or frontend components. Implementing this would require adding an `alt_text` (or similar) parameter to the Python API for each affected element, extending the corresponding protobuf messages, and updating the frontend components to render the provided alt text. The relationship between `st.image`'s existing `caption` parameter and the new alt text would need to be defined (caption is visual, alt text is for screen readers). ### Related Issues - **[#12873 - 508 Compliance - Add Alt="" tag to decorative elements](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/12873)**: Closely related accessibility request focused on adding empty `alt=""` to *decorative* elements (like icons in selectboxes) to prevent screen reader clutter. This issue (#8563) covers adding *descriptive* alt text to content elements like images and charts — complementary but distinct scope. - **[#8399 - Basic accessibility web features](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/8399)**: Broader request for basic web accessibility features (page lang attribute, accessible link naming, structural compliance). Alt text for images/charts would fall under this umbrella of accessibility improvements. - **[#10119 - Fullscreen label for `st.image`](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/10119)**: Request to add descriptive labels/context to images in fullscreen mode. While focused on visual descriptions rather than screen reader accessibility, both involve adding metadata/descriptions to `st.image` and could share implementation patterns. --- *This is an automated triage comment using `opus-4.6-thinking`. Please verify the suggested labels and related issues.*

Closing this as completed.

**What shipped**: keyword-only `alt=` so authors can give an accessible name to the surfaces this issue called for — `st.image`, `st.dataframe` / `st.table`, and the chart commands — plus related media and embeds covered by the approved product spec ([#16937](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/16937) / specs/2026-09-14-element-alt-text/product-spec.md).

**Representative PRs**: [#16568](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/16568) (audio/video), [#17040](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/17040) (iframe), [#17041](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/17041) (altair_chart, vega_lite_chart), [#17069](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/17069) (line_chart, bar_chart, area_chart, scatter_chart), [#17080](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/17080) (echarts_chart), [#17081](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/17081) (plotly_chart), [#17085](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/17085) (graphviz_chart), [#17086](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/17086) (map, pydeck_chart), [#17095](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/17095) (table), [#17096](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/17096) (mermaid_chart), [#17118](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/17118) (pdf), [#17125](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/17125) (dataframe/data_editor), [#17136](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/17136) & [#17137](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/17137) (image/pyplot). Agent guidance: [#17201](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/17201).

`caption` stays the visible label on `st.image`; alt is the assistive name (independent, including decorative `alt=""` on image/pyplot only).
